Why Were They Flagged?  ·  High-Priority Signals
About This Analysis Proof of Concept  ·  Three things to know
Condition ratings reflect field inspections
The High / Medium / Low ratings for the 81,832 inspected roads come directly from field-measured Pavement Condition Index (PCI) scores — not from the model. The model is only applied to the 31,961 roads that have never been inspected.
Most predicted roads show "Schedule Repair" due to incomplete records
87% of uninspected roads are predicted as Medium priority because key attributes — road type, width, and age — are missing from city records for those segments. This is a data completeness gap, not a model limitation. Filling in those records would sharpen predictions.
Predicted priorities guide inspections, not spending
Predictions for uninspected roads are based on structural characteristics such as road type, age, and maintenance history — not direct condition measurement. They are intended to prioritise which roads to inspect next, and should not be used to commit capital expenditure without a field inspection first.
